). Aram-zobah--Syria of Zobah (
), to whose king the king of the former was tributary. The war with Edom, by Joab and Abishai (

).

entries.title: Psalms 60:3
segments: 3. drink ... wine of astonishment--literally, "of staggering"--that is, made us weak (compare

entries.title: Psalms 60:4
segments: 4, 5. Yet to God's banner they will rally, and pray that, led and sustained by His power (right hand,
), they may be safe.

entries.title: Psalms 60:5
segments: 5. hear me--or, "hear us."

entries.title: Psalms 60:6
segments:
6-10. God hath spoken in--or, "by." 
 
    his holiness-- (
), on the pledge of His attributes (
). Taking courage from God's promise to give them possession (

) (and perhaps renewed to him by special revelation), with triumphant joy he describes the conquest as already made. 
 
    Shechem, and ... Succoth--as widely separated points, and--

entries.title: Psalms 60:7
segments:
7. Gilead ... and Manasseh--as large districts, east and west of Jordan, represent the whole land. 
 
    divide ... and mete out--means to have entire control over. 
 
    Ephraim--denotes the military (

); and-- 
 
    Judah--(the lawgiver,
), the civil power. Foreign nations are then presented as subdued.

entries.title: Psalms 60:8
segments:
8. Moab--is a my washpot--the most ordinary vessel. 
 
    over--or, "at" 
 
    Edom--(as a slave) he casts his shoe. 
 
    Philistia, triumph, &c.--or, rather, "shout." 
 
    for me--acknowledges subjection (compare
, "over Philistia will I triumph").

entries.title: Psalms 60:9
segments:
9, 10. He feels assured that, though once angry, God is now ready to favor His people. 
 
    who will lead me-- or, who has led me, as if the work were now begun.

entries.title: Psalms 60:10
segments: 10. Wilt not thou?--or, "Is it not Thou?"

entries.title: Psalms 60:11
segments: 11, 12. Hence he closes with a prayer for success, and an assurance of a hearing.
